page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor using the arm64 ARMv9 architecture. Each dedicated vCPU corresponds to one physical core operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz without simultaneous multithreading, supported by 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache. The instance features 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per core. For high-speed temporary data access, it includes 3800 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and delivers 30 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. Discrete GPUs are not present on this instance type.

Benchmark evaluations reveal substantial throughput across multi-threaded operations and high-bandwidth memory sub-systems. In synthetic and application workloads, the c8gd.16xlarge achieves top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core execution (25,249.0) and Clang compilation (81,908.0), alongside strong multi-core stress-ng performance (109,160.43). Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 459.25 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaches 196.82 GB/sec, placing memory throughput in the top decile. In database-related benchmarks, it produces 133.11 million Redis SET operations per second and top-tier PassMark database scores. Conversely, single-threaded metrics, including Geekbench single-core (1,890.0) and gzip compression (30.22 GB/sec), fall into the average tier, showing that the system favors parallel execution over single-thread clock frequency.

By combining high physical core density with bundled high-capacity NVMe storage, the instance provides high operational efficiency for I/O-heavy parallel jobs without incurring the latency or cost overhead of external block storage. The platform is suited for multi-threaded build systems, distributed caching tiers like Redis, batch ETL data pipelines, high-throughput static web serving, and database workloads requiring high local storage speeds.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gd.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by a 64-core ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz with dedicated physical cores. It provides 128.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core), 3800 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, and 30 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth without discrete GPUs. Benchmark results indicate exceptional multi-core and memory throughput, scoring in the top tier for Clang compilation (81,908.0), Geekbench multi-core (25,249.0), PassMark database operations, and Redis SET throughput reaching 133.11 million operations per second. While single-thread execution falls into the middle tier, the high physical core count and massive memory bandwidth of 459.25 GB/sec deliver robust resource density. These characteristics make the instance effective for parallel software build pipelines, distributed caching layers, data transformation pipelines, and high-concurrency web serving.
